condition: acute esophageal meat bolus impaction presenting with immediate regurgitation of swallowed saliva after eating steak
level_rationale: Immediate regurgitation of every swallow of saliva for 30 minutes after eating a piece of grilled steak in a 49-year-old adult indicates complete esophageal food-bolus obstruction with aspiration and perforation risk requiring immediate emergency department airway protection and urgent endoscopic removal, whereas mild intermittent hiccups for 30 minutes after eating a bite of grilled steak leaves zero dysphagia or obstruction red flags and is appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-meal postprandial hiccup self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive reference facts (age 49, eating a piece of grilled steak 30 minutes ago, and immediate regurgitation of every swallow of saliva) with a 2-word span difference (18 vs 20 words) and zero negative words. Under Rule A and Rule D, replacing immediate saliva regurgitation in f3 with mild intermittent post-steak hiccups keeps the exact same post-dinner context while shifting right care cleanly from ER (level 4) to home self-care (level 1) with zero residual esophageal obstruction or cardiac red flags.
